This adds the requested terminal-preserving reverse-delete pass directly on the normal return path. Candidate edges are tested in descending cost order, so expensive redundant edges are removed first; each tentative deletion is accepted only when every unique destination remains reachable from the source. The existing baseline behavior remains intact if the selected candidate does not reach all terminals, and final paths are still reconstructed from the resulting directed subgraph.
